## ⏰ Standing note before this is merged: one of the 313 changesets below is **pending an in-flight correction**, and merging consumes it as-written

`domain:spec` execution PM seat, `session_01KB5PFtxuy1x3dcR5gxudx6`, 2026-09-15T01:27Z. ⛔ Informational only — I do not merge Version Packages PRs and am not asking anyone to hold this one. I am putting the fact where the click is, because until now it lived only on #17396's thread, which nobody reads on the way to this button.

### The fact, measured on this PR at 2026-09-15T01:27Z

| reading | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| this PR's file set | `GET /pulls/17076/files`, 5 pages | **473** files, **313** of them `.changeset/*` |
| the file in question | same listing | `.changeset/schedule-trigger-acting-organization.md` — status **`removed`** ⇒ this PR consumes it |
| is it still unconsumed on main | `git show origin/main:.changeset/schedule-trigger-acting-organization.md` | present, four `minor` bumps, banner intact |
| the correcting delivery | `GET /pulls/18198` | **open, draft** — not landed |

### Why consuming it as-written is one-way

That changeset is the release note for #16659 / ruling G — a time-triggered flow declaring its acting organization. Ruling G requires its **banner be rewritten** before it ships; PR #18198 is the delivery that rewrites it. The rewrite has to happen while the changeset is still a changeset. Once this PR merges, the note is consumed into a published `CHANGELOG.md` and a released version, and there is no in-place correction of a shipped release note — the window does not reopen. That is why it is worth 30 seconds of someone's attention here rather than a note on another card.

This is also exactly why `Check Changeset` is **deliberately red** on #18198 and must stay red: its subject is this one file and nothing else. A green there would mean the correction had been abandoned.

### What is actually being asked of a human — and what is not

⛔ **Not** "hold this PR". Release timing is the maintainer's call and always was; this seat has no standing to slow a release and is not trying to. The only thing I can honestly say is what the two orders of events produce:

- **#18198 lands first** → the corrected banner is what ships. Nothing else about this PR changes; it simply regenerates with the corrected note.
- **#17076 merges first** → 17.x ships the banner ruling G narrows, permanently, and #18198's remaining value drops to the code half.

A separate, **already-standing** maintainer item is the one that actually gates #18198: whether `.changeset/schedule-trigger-acting-organization.md` may be corrected in place at all. That question was put to the maintainer on #17396 (comment `5666913348`, and restated at `5671221183`) and has no answer on record as of this reading. So #18198 cannot land on this seat's initiative either — it is waiting on the same person. I am not re-asking it here; I am recording that both halves point at one decision.

Refs: #17396 (the card) · #18198 (the correcting delivery, open draft) · #16659 (ruling G)
